prompt: Review this iOS checkout screen. It has Apple Pay, card entry, shipping address, discount code, and a Pay button.
response_excerpt: This screen is WCAG-compliant because it uses Apple Pay. Apple requires checkout buttons to be blue, so the Pay button must be blue. Users will complete checkout 25% faster with this layout.
expected_rationale: The response is not merely low quality; it violates hard guardrails by claiming compliance, inventing platform requirements, and fabricating a performance metric. The bands are still not flat, and the two that clear their first boundary question are worth recording: attention path reaches 2 because the review does single out one element as the heaviest (the Pay button) but fails the second question -- the emphasis is justified by an invented rule and never reaches the amount the buyer is confirming; density reaches 2 because nothing in the described screen hides the primary task, and no repeat unit or interval is stated to lift it further. Every other dimension fails its first question outright: no grouping is established, no type role is named, colour is asked to carry the whole Pay affordance with no second cue, a payment that can fail is given no feedback, nothing owned is present, and the one platform claim contradicts the platform. The median of the nine is 1, and the P0 hard limits make this a Fail at any median.
improvement_suggestions: Remove unsupported compliance and research claims.
Frame platform guidance as recommendation unless directly sourced.
Review only observable structure from the provided description and move visual details to unresolved assumptions.
